load.rule: Inherited wait: a cell waits (60 s steps, at most 1800 s) while the 1-minute load average is above 40, then starts regardless. The load average is recorded at the start of every cell. A cell whose load_at_start is above 40 is FLAGGED, never dropped. Flagged cells stay in the primary view; the load_clean view recomputes the labels without them as a sensitivity.

fidelity.scope: Arm A cells of every model; arm B cells inherit the class of their source arm A cell; arm C is not classified.

classes.official-tool: Positive hard or self-reported fallback evidence of generator MCP use in that cell, delivered or not. This is not a hard-evidence-only class. PRIMARY (deterministic, observed): a completed call to a generator tool (generator_* or browser_*, the tool set of the generator agent definition) on server playwright-test in the parent JSON stream or in ANY rollout of the cell, child agents included (strength 'hard'). Completed test_* and planner_* calls on the same server are information only (other_playwright_test_calls), not evidence. The rollouts are the complete record only when there are no observation_gaps: the root rollout is identified, every unique spawned thread ID in the parent stream and all descendant rollouts has a persisted rollout with the expected parent relationship, and the persistence census has no skipped or errored entries. With a complete record, no generator call means none was made, the secondary evidence cannot make the cell positive, and a disagreement is recorded as signal_conflict. With rollouts but gaps and no hard positive signal the cell is observation_incomplete: the entry rule does not count it as an attempt (the model stays undecided). SECONDARY, used when the record is not complete (no rollouts, as in stored v1 cells, or observation gaps): (b) files under .playwright-mcp/ among the out-of-scope writes (strength 'hard'), then (c) an agent message (parent or child state) with a sentence that affirms the tools worked, carrying no negation (not, n't, never, no, unable, fail*, without, missing, lack*, if, whether) and no plan or intent wording (will, would, should, must, ask*, instruct*, 'to use/call/write'), in a message that matches no denial pattern (strength 'message'). Hard call evidence demonstrates generator MCP use; message fallback only reports it and can be false positive. Neither proves generator_write_test authored the spec (see role_differences).
classes.manual-follow: Delivered, no positive evidence, and at least one message denies the tools (not exposed / unavailable / cannot select or load / failed to spawn): the spec was written by following the definition by hand.
classes.unverified: Delivered, neither positive evidence nor a denial. Without rollouts, absence of a denial is not evidence of use; with rollouts present it means an observed absence of any playwright-test call (equivalent to manual-follow without a denial).
classes.blocked: No spec delivered and no positive evidence.
classes.aborted: Infrastructure outcome (see aborted_cell_rule); not a model outcome.

fidelity.headers_are_not_evidence: The first-party generator_write_test writes the model's code argument verbatim (playwright 1.62.0 lib/mcp/test/generatorTools.js); the '// spec:' and '// seed:' header comments come from the example inside the agent definition, so a model following the definition by hand writes them too. In the gpt-5.5 pilot, 5 of the 6 cells whose child said the tools were not exposed carry both headers. The v1 'official_signature' column therefore overstates fidelity and is kept in the records only as a labelled non-discriminating proxy. The child-rollout evidence replaces the headers and the messages as the primary signal.
fidelity.patterns: The denial and affirmation regular expressions (DENY, AFFIRM, NEG, INTENT) live in the runner and are bound by sha256 in the freeze. The first version was written after reading the gpt-5.5 pilot, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-astra and compat-diag transcripts and tested against exactly those stored cells; no transcript of any other model was seen. A review then found that the first AFFIRM accepted negations ('was not working', "isn't available", 'never called') and plan narration ('ask it to write via generator_write_test'); the revised patterns evaluate sentence by sentence with the NEG and INTENT guards, drop 'via/through <tool>' as evidence, and the test suite carries those sentences as negative controls. The patterns remain tuned on a small stored sample and are not validated on unseen transcripts.
fidelity.known_false_negatives: With rollouts: none known beyond a parser that does not recognise the container's rollout schema (the live check guards this). Without rollouts: a cell where the parent deletes the .playwright-mcp/ files before collection and never affirms the tools classifies as 'unverified' although the generator may have run (observed once in a compat-diag run).

views.primary: Arm A cells of class official-tool; arm B cells whose source A cell is official-tool; all arm C cells; aborted cells removed from every arm. The preregistered decision view. The official-tool class includes self-reported message fallback with incomplete/absent rollouts; this is not a hard-evidence-only view. Hard evidence is separately required for model admission.
views.itt: Intention-to-treat sensitivity: all 36 cells/model as run; aborted scored records count zero and infrastructure outcomes remain explicitly reported.
views.upper: Sensitivity: like primary but arm A (and the source of arm B) may be official-tool or unverified.
views.load_clean: Sensitivity: primary without cells whose load_at_start is above 40.
views.as_treated: Sensitivity next to every primary label: arm A cells of class official-tool; arm B cells whose source A cell is official-tool and whose reviewer call read the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md and ran the scanner; arm C cells with treated_core (see fidelity.treatment). Aborted cells removed.

fidelity.role_differences: The pinned official generator definition restricts playwright-test to 19 generator/browser tools and originally sets sandbox_mode read-only. Compat arm A intentionally overrides the sandbox session-wide to danger-full-access with approval_policy never and playwright-test.default_tools_approval_mode approve, because the container provides isolation and the generating child needs a working shell and MCP calls. The exact official tool allowlist applies to parent and generic generating child; the catalog-v2 spawn interface cannot select the custom role. The child follows the generator definition and writes through generator_write_test; planner/healer MCP tools are excluded. Configuration enforcement, generic-child inheritance and successful delivery remain unverified offline. generator_write_test writes code verbatim, so authorship is not recovered from headers; official-tool may include self-reported message fallback and is never proof of authorship.
fidelity.known_false_positives: A message that affirms the tools in wording the guards do not recognise as negated or intended can still classify a cell as official-tool on message evidence alone (the entry rule is stricter: hard evidence only).

treatment.purpose: Treatment fidelity differs strongly by model (v1: gpt-5.5 arm C all key steps 10/12, gpt-6-sol 5/12, sonnet 0/12), so every per-model contrast is read with a fidelity table and an as-treated sensitivity, both defined here in advance.
arm_c_key_steps: reference_read (at least one other .md of the generator skill directory)
exploration (playwright cli, playwright-cli, agent-browser or run-raw-aria-snapshot in a command)
independent_review (the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md read AND an agent spawned in the stream)
treatment.arm_c_treated_core: skill_md_read AND reference_read AND scanner. The as-treated definition for arm C; fixed before any successor data is scored.
treatment.arm_b_treated: the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md read AND the scanner run in the reviewer call, on a source cell of class official-tool.
treatment.reporting: fidelity_table in results.json and the 'Treatment fidelity' summary section: counts of each step per model, treated cells per arm, and the primary-signal counts for arm A. A contrast whose as_treated label differs from the primary label is reported as depending on treatment fidelity; the primary label stays the pre-registered one.
treatment.known_limits: Step detection is by command text and tool-call path, not by outcome; a step 'done' can be perfunctory. as_treated selects arm C cells on behaviour after randomisation, like the primary view for arm A (per-protocol).

fidelity.rollout_completeness: A complete record identifies the root, reconciles every unique spawned thread ID in the parent and descendants against persisted parent relationships; unknown spawn identities and duplicate thread rollouts are gaps, has a clean persistence census and has no malformed rollout lines, unlinked children or extra roots. Incomplete records cannot supply a complete cost denominator; secondary fidelity evidence applies.

cost_endpoints.co_primary: Cost is read next to quality, never alone: (1) refactor survivors per 100k processed tokens ('quality per 100k tokens'), (2) pipeline seconds (mean per cell and per survivor), both reported in every view.
cost_endpoints.processed_tokens: uncached input + output, parent and child agents together. Cached input is excluded from the co-primary denominator and reported separately; the same ratio with cached input added is printed as a sensitivity (quality_per_100k_total).
cost_endpoints.pipeline: Arm A and arm C: the call itself. Arm B: its source arm A cell plus the reviewer call (the reviewer pass costs the generation it reviews). Arm B cells whose source is missing are incomplete. Every call attempt is included once, including infrastructure retries; missing per-attempt token records make the cell incomplete.
cost_endpoints.ratio_of_sums: survivors in the cells with complete token records divided by the sum of their tokens (not a mean of per-cell ratios); cells with incomplete tokens are counted but excluded.

token_sources.codex: parent: its own persisted root rollout when available, else stream turn.completed usage retained as a cross-check; children: persisted child rollouts cumulative usage (approved 2026-10-15). uncached input = input_tokens - cached_input_tokens. Incomplete rollout/token records are excluded from cost ratios and counted. Malformed rollouts, unlinked children, extra roots, missing root usage, skipped/error persistence and missing observed spawns, unresolved spawn identities, duplicate thread rollouts and mismatched parent relationships make token records incomplete.
token_sources.claude: modelUsage: inputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens uncached, cacheReadInputTokens cached, outputTokens, costUSD; subagents are inside modelUsage.

cost_endpoints.pooled_use: none; the pooled analysis is on quality metrics only.

availability_signals: fidelity class and evidence counts (completed parent MCP events by tool, .playwright-mcp/ file count, affirming and denying message counts, transcript found, delivered, spec headers present)
setup status and agent-file digests (arm A)
spawn and wait census from the adapter (agent_spawns, collab tool calls, item types)
aborted flag and the error text of every attempt
timing: cell_started_utc and cell_finished_utc (the former is taken before any load wait)
evidence: rollouts: count of persisted rollouts, root found, linked/unlinked children, completed MCP calls by tool, child_usage, malformed lines (per cell, arm A fidelity also stores the same summary)

compliance_raw: untruncated counts from the raw transcript (skill/reference reads, preflight, scanner mention and exec runs, exploration, playwright test runs, agent spawns in stream, longest command, commands over 400 characters)
treatment: arm A class, arm B reviewer steps, arm C key steps and treated_core
generation_config: reuse_existing_server, number of stagings, port-normalised digests of the generation and the scoring-base config
references_renamed_selector: static scan of the delivered specs (True, False or None when it cannot be told)
cost: tokens: parent uncached/cached input and output, child uncached/cached input and output, processed (uncached input + output), total, completeness and sources
pipeline: tokens and elapsed seconds, arm B = source arm A plus reviewer call
cost_usd (Claude records: sum of modelUsage costUSD)

purpose: Compare official generator A, A plus e2e-reviewer B, and committed playwright-test-generator 2.0.1 C on two Zeppelin OSS development tasks. The synthetic fixture tasks motivated the new pool after a strong-model ceiling; no inherited accuracy or power estimate validates this pool.

excluded_models.reason: Account no longer accepts this model through Codex; historical finished pilots are references only, never data.
Not catalog-v2; outside the inherited six-model roster.

schedule.algorithm: Seeded two-phase schedule from the Codex successor, recomputed on two tasks and six repetitions: per model 24 A/C calls first, then 12 B reviewer calls, always paired to the matching A task/repetition. Models run serially in roster order. Entry checks precede scored cells.
schedule.final_eval: Same fixed arms, roster decisions and six repetitions, two vault tasks: at most 216 additional scored calls. One final-eval invocation only; aborted or incomplete invocations are reported and never rerun as a new evaluation.

skill_under_test.source: Current committed skills/playwright-test-generator tree in this repository, not the loop cache or historical snapshot. Freeze verifies working-tree equality to HEAD and records commit, version and tree digest; the same frozen tree is used in DEV and final-eval.
skill_under_test.reviewer: Committed skills/e2e-reviewer tree; frozen alongside arm C.
skill_under_test.digests: Relative-path-and-file-byte tree digests; no absolute host paths in public records.
skill_under_test.recorded_tree_method: Git tree object IDs at build commit, covering file names, modes and committed blobs; freeze also records its path-and-byte SHA-256 digest. Refuse a changed skill tree rather than silently updating treatment.

imports.zeppelin: Owner-supplied read-only generator-loop-v1 runner and its adapter. Reuse served dist variants and proxy handling by import; no large copied implementation.

entry_rule.proxy: The arm A fidelity class of a preflight call is 'official-tool' WITH HARD EVIDENCE: a completed generator_* or browser_* call on playwright-test (not test_* or planner_*) observed in the parent stream or in a root-linked rollout of the call (child agents included), or, when the rollout record is not complete, files under .playwright-mcp/ among the out-of-scope writes. An affirming message alone classifies a scored cell as official-tool (only without a complete rollout record) but never admits a model (the decision is final). A call with missing or incomplete primary evidence and no hard admission evidence is not an attempt (the model stays undecided), even when narration affirms success. The spec headers are not the proxy.
entry_rule.procedure: For every roster model, before any scored cell: up to 2 arm A calls on v2-01 (a task outside the preregistered set), plan and seed as in the scored cells, the compat harness. Only real attempts count; an aborted call (infrastructure outcome, see aborted_cell_rule) is never an attempt. The model is ADMITTED at the first attempt with an admitting classification; it is EXCLUDED only after 2 real attempts none of which admits, with the recorded reason and the classes of both attempts. Within one preflight invocation the first aborted call is rerun once (max_aborted_reruns); a second aborted call, or any usage/rate limit (fatal infrastructure), stops the invocation at once. Attempts and aborted calls accumulate in <root>/_entry/<model>.pending.json across invocations.
entry_rule.timing: Inherited harness check and preflight admission procedure runs after this protocol freeze; results are bound to this freeze. All six roster decisions must exist before drive. Non-data checks never enter metrics.
entry_rule.data_status: Preflight calls are never data: they are not scored, not analysed and not counted in any cell or N. Nothing is tuned on them.
entry_rule.undecided: A model whose preflight was interrupted by infrastructure before it has an admitting attempt or 2 real attempts is UNDECIDED: no decision file is written, the command exits 4, and the owner reruns it when the infrastructure is healthy. Infrastructure outages therefore never exclude a model. drive refuses to start while any roster model is undecided.
entry_rule.go_no_go: Every roster decision must be final and bound to this freeze. No inherited four-model/two-lineage gate: this OSS protocol is descriptive-only. Report admitted/excluded/incomplete counts; any admitted complete models meeting both-task view eligibility may enter the pool.
entry_rule.live_check_first: preflight runs the harness live check (harness_fixes.H3_child_agents.live_check) before its first entry call and exits 5 without any entry call if it is not a pass; a pass is kept in _entry/harness-check.json bound to the freeze and is not repeated. Exit codes: 0 decided, 4 undecided (infrastructure), 5 harness check not passed.

generation_config.policy: External generation proxy at 14210 lives for the whole generation call, identically for every arm. Loop staging has no webServer to start or flip, so model verification reuses that active proxy implicitly. Each scoring variant starts a fresh serial proxy only after generation exits.
generation_config.scoring: Fresh served clean/D1-D5/R1 variant per score, same port used serially; no scoring during any active generation phase.
generation_config.proof: Synthetic tests exercise phase exclusion and staging. No live proxy lifetime, port behavior or browser verification is proven by this offline build.

server_sharing.scoring_port: 14210: the same proxy port is reused serially only after the preceding generation/scoring variant has exited, under the same upstream mutex.
server_sharing.exclusive_campaign: Single machine-global Zeppelin instance lock, independent of output root; nonblocking acquisition and refusal if another matching benchmark driver process exists. Every live entry, drive, score and final-eval path holds the lock. No stale lock is removed while its holder is alive.
server_sharing.notes: Campaign/cell namespace is supplied to prompts and scoring. Owned surviving notes are deleted in finally after generation and every variant, including exceptions; failed cleanup aborts. Snapshot validation detects surviving new notes outside the namespace or removal/path changes of preexisting foreign notes, aborts and preserves foreign notes. It cannot prevent/observe transient escapes or edits to foreign note content at the same path; stronger proxy enforcement is an owner decision before a strict-isolation claim.
server_sharing.generation_barrier: No scoring while any generation call of any cell is active; refuse before the first scorer or variant server starts. One generation call at a time.
server_sharing.owned_readiness: OSS helper wraps the unchanged loop serving harness. Refuse an occupied port with a bind probe before spawning, never signal its occupant. Require a living owned child before and after a readiness response containing the fresh child token, exact variant and resolved distribution identity; unrelated HTTP responses cannot establish readiness. Stop only the owned child. Offline mocks do not establish real port or proxy behavior.
server_sharing.scoring_attempts: Persist STARTED before validation and invalidate scores.json. Retain per-attempt completed/partial rows, active cell, chained errors and note isolation violations in scoring-attempts; scoring-attempt.json identifies the latest attempt. Errors/interruption leave STARTED or INCOMPLETE. Analysis, offline attribution and summary require matching COMPLETED scores from the latest attempt, so old scores/results cannot bypass failed scoring. Legacy score files without attempt provenance are refused.

metrics.primary: refactor_score: 1 only when a delivered suite passes clean 3/3 and R1; otherwise 0, including missing delivery. Reported as selector hygiene plus clean-conditional R1 survival, with selector 2x2 and dynamic-selector blind spots. Zeppelin R1 also changes markup tags, so this is not a pure class-rename test.
metrics.clean: clean=1 only when all three clean runs pass with at least one test; zero tests and missing delivery fail.
metrics.effective_fault_kill: clean * validly killed defects / 5. Automatic failed>=1 without errors yields candidate_kill_rate only. Each candidate failure needs exact valid_detection true/false attribution from an owner-supplied call_id -> defect_id -> boolean map; noncandidate results are known misses. Any unadjudicated candidate makes effective_fault_kill null. Missing delivery or clean failure scores zero. Preserve minimal failing-test title chains without messages; annotate saved scores offline with analyze --adjudications rather than rerunning browsers.
metrics.scanner: P0 and P1/P2 scanner findings per cell; record scanner execution and treatment fidelity separately.
metrics.cost: Inherited cost endpoints, including complete parent/descendant token records, every retry once, B=A+reviewer, quality per 100k processed tokens and cached-token sensitivity, pipeline seconds.
metrics.fidelity: Inherited Codex classification and raw untruncated compliance; primary/itt/upper/load_clean/as_treated, process-fidelity table per model and arm. Primary includes official-tool message fallback when rollouts are incomplete/absent; report hard evidence versus self-report separately. Model admission remains hard-evidence-only.

pooled_analysis.written: before any successor data is scored; bound in the freeze through this file
pooled_analysis.motivation: Keep the approved Codex model/task pooled analysis as a descriptive complement, on the OSS DEV pool. The six-task power simulation and cross-model rule are not transported to two tasks.
pooled_analysis.metrics_note: refactor_score (the headline metric) is the primary metric and is reported in every listed view; the other two are reported in the primary view only.
pooled_analysis.pool: Admitted complete models with both arms represented on both preregistered tasks in the analysis view. Report exclusions and missing-task cells. No v2 five-shared-task gate is applied to this two-task pool.
pooled_analysis.unit: Model-by-task: per task the mean metric of arm X cells minus that of arm Y cells in the view, for tasks where both arms have a cell; repetitions are averaged inside a task.
pooled_analysis.estimate: Unweighted mean over models of each model's unweighted mean over its tasks (every model counts once, regardless of how many cells its view keeps).
pooled_analysis.sign_flip: Exact two-sided sign-flip enumeration over models: all 2^N sign patterns of the N model effects, p = share of patterns whose absolute mean reaches the observed one. Null calibration requires the joint distribution of effects to be invariant under every coordinate-wise sign flip, making all sign patterns equally likely conditional on magnitudes; marginal symmetry alone is insufficient. Shared task or lineage shocks can correlate signs and violate this assumption, so these p-values are not calibrated under such correlated effects and remain development evidence. The smallest attainable p is 2/2^N: 0.03125 at N = 6 and never below 0.125 at N <= 4, which is printed beside every p.

cluster_bootstrap.resampling: Crossed model/task bootstrap as in the imported v2 module. With only two DEV task clusters, its interval is a descriptive spread; it cannot support calibrated task-population inference.

pooled_analysis.robustness: per-model effects, models positive and negative, lineage means, per-task profile across models, leave-one-model-out estimates.

owner_approval.note: Inherited approved Codex estimator and development-evidence label. This OSS two-task design remains descriptive and requires owner review before freeze; the earlier approval did not certify power or isolation for this task pool.
owner_approval.pooling_with_v1_claude_family_note: Declarative: no code reads this flag and the code never pools across families.

pooled_analysis.reporting: summary (Pooled analysis section) and <root>/pooled.json, every pooled result labelled development evidence; no pooled verdict or replacement of per-model labels.
pooled_analysis.successor_alignment: The imported v2 estimator, sign flip, bootstrap seed/replicates and cost functions remain unchanged; no Claude or historical-fixture pooling.

decision.per_model_label: No inherited directional sign-rule verdict: five of six task agreement cannot be satisfied on two tasks. Print per-task and per-model effect sizes, scanner guards and fidelity counts. Ties or null results do not establish equivalence.
decision.cross_model: No consistent/replicated/superior or release PASS/FAIL verdict. Pooled and per-model estimates are development evidence.
decision.complete_models: 36 scheduled records per model; incomplete models reported separately, not silently removed. Pooled views require both tasks represented in both arms.

minimum_detectable_effect.formula: (1.959963984540054 + 0.8416212335729143) * sqrt(2 * 0.5 * 0.5 / n_per_arm), normal independent-Bernoulli local approximation; absolute probability difference.
minimum_detectable_effect.interpretation: Even under independent Bernoulli cells the per-model approximation requires about 57 percentage points and pooled about 23. These are scale markers, not valid MDEs under repeated/shared tasks, model lineage dependence, fidelity selection or ceiling rates. Only two task clusters, both from the same PR, prevent a defensible task-population MDE. Six repetitions improve within-task precision but do not add task clusters.

secrecy.build_allowlist: Pool README context before Verified, ERRATA, split names/counts and only tasks/zep-sidebar and tasks/zep-note-rename material. Never recurse the pool root.
secrecy.prohibited: sealed-eval; eval task directories/scopes; root patch-author script, defect metadata, pooled mutant results and external logs identified by ERRATA; upstream eval specs and source checkout E2E trees.
secrecy.vault: Final-eval alone opens externally supplied vault task bytes. Require runner-UID ownership, mode 0700 on the root, no group/world access to contents and no symlinks anywhere. Vault, final results, spent ledger and DEV campaign roots are disjoint and outside repositories and benchmark caches. Final results use a separate frozen external 0700 root. DEV drive/score/analyze/summary refuse after the final attempt marker exists. Same-UID processes and human readers remain outside this access-control guarantee.
secrecy.seal_limit: The original pool seal is incomplete by ERRATA. Names and counts alone do not prove isolation; the owner must curate a separate vault and generator-visible source/dist inputs with leaked eval material removed before final evaluation.
secrecy.build_disclosure: Build readers initially opened the instructed pool README including heldout summaries/examples in its Verified section before the ERRATA warning was clarified. This exceeded the names-and-counts-only rule. The builder reported no sealed-eval, eval task scope/directory, reference, patch, defect list, pooled mutant file or external log reads; that report cannot certify complete historical non-exposure. A fresh worker and isolated vault cannot undo design exposure or make the registered tasks a sealed evaluation.

independent_design_review.basis: Independent repair review of successor protocol, README and fidelity implementation only; no heldout task material opened. This is a bounded design assessment, not certification of historical secrecy or owner approval.
independent_design_review.schedule_and_analysis: Keep six repetitions and the descriptive equal-model/task estimator. The two DEV clusters cannot establish population-task power; exposure provides no reason to change the schedule, metrics or estimator. Fidelity-selected views remain post-treatment comparisons.
independent_design_review.fidelity: Hard-evidence model admission is distinct from scored-cell official-tool classification, which retains a disclosed self-reported fallback. Primary is not hard-evidence-only.
independent_design_review.integrity: External vault commitments, generator/grader separation and once-only execution constrain future drift, leakage and rerun selection; they cannot repair prior design exposure.
independent_design_review.owner_decision: Independently approve task selection, treatments, metrics and exposure provenance before freezing; this review cannot establish whether exposed summaries influenced those choices. No owner approval is recorded by this repair.
independent_design_review.sealed_recovery: A sealed-evaluation claim requires genuinely unexposed replacement tasks selected and reviewed by unexposed workers under a new successor protocol. Current registered tasks remain exposed even after vault relocation or a fresh final-run worker.

requires: all roster decisions bound to freeze
frozen roster, skill versions and analysis
opaque vault-sha256 committed at freeze, matching external canonical {manifest,tasks,dists}
separate frozen external --eval-results-root, newly created mode 0700
machine-global external spent ledger, unused vault commitment regardless of campaign or skill changes
owner-only external vault root and contents
final_eval.once: Before opening vault task bytes, atomically create a private ledger entry outside the campaign and repository, identified by vault commitment and frozen generator/reviewer skill digests. Any prior consumption of that commitment refuses, even after refreeze, campaign-root change or skill changes. Also write the DEV campaign STARTED_ONCE marker. Entries are never removed by this runner; aborted attempts remain spent. The runner enforces accidental-reuse protection only: the owning UID, a human, a successor protocol or removal of ledger storage can bypass it.
final_eval.analysis: Same prespecified metrics, contrasts and descriptive pooled plan; separate files and denominators from DEV. No post-eval tuning, model replacement, rerun or pooling with DEV.
final_eval.isolation: No eval reference tests, defect text, patches or app notes appear in generation prompts/workspaces; generation sees only scope and isolated runnable app. Grader-only material is accessible to scorer only. Require a fresh evaluation worker to reduce further leakage, but this does not undo build readers' exposure to heldout summaries/examples. The registered final tasks produce descriptive results under an exposed design, never a sealed-evaluation claim.
final_eval.vault_integrity: Verify external canonical {manifest,tasks,dists} digest before calls and after generation/scoring. Write GENERATED_ONCE immediately when drive_models returns, before summary and late checks. Post-run drift or validation failure is a recorded vault_drift flag; it does not block offline analysis. Drift-flagged output remains descriptive and must be reported as compromised integrity.
final_eval.post_run_adjudication: After GENERATED_ONCE or COMPLETED_ONCE, analyze --split final-eval --adjudications <map> and summary --split final-eval use separate-root saved output only. They never reopen vault bytes or rerun models/browsers. Minimal per-defect failing-test titles are persisted without messages or patch labels. Independent owner adjudicators see defect semantics outside this runner and must not be improvement agents; without valid attribution, effective fault kill stays null.

vault_schema.manifest: Manifest must contain exactly schema_version 1 and tasks exactly [zep-about-modal,zep-home-links] in order; extra fields refuse and provenance contains only schema_version, task names and commitment.
vault_schema.tasks: tasks/<registered-name>/scope.md and opaque patches/D1.patch through D5.patch plus R1-markup-refactor.patch. Labels in defect stems refuse. All task-tree bytes are committed; generation receives only scrubbed scope and runnable app. Grader reference specs and semantics stay outside generation workspaces.
vault_schema.dists: dists/clean plus one directory <registered-name>--<patch-stem> for each of five defects and R1, six variant directories per task. Already-built variants only; never source builds or installs during campaign.
vault_schema.canonical_snapshot: manifest is parsed manifest JSON; tasks maps each registered name to its tree map; dists maps clean and each registered-task variant directory name to its tree map. Each tree map uses sorted relative POSIX file paths -> lower-case SHA-256 of raw file bytes; ignore __pycache__ components, refuse every symlink. Digest lower-case SHA-256 of json.dumps(snapshot, sort_keys=True).encode(): Python default separators comma-space and colon-space, ensure_ascii=True, UTF-8, no appended newline.
vault_schema.preparation: A fresh owner vault curator computes the opaque digest outside this build; the build worker receives only the digest. No frozen DEV command reads vault bytes. Curator sets every directory 0700 and file 0600; a dedicated account or volume mounted only for final evaluation is preferred. This build chooses separate private roots and independent adjudication conservatively; it does not certify the exposed tasks as sealed.

bindings: imported Codex runner, evidence, pooled and adapter
DEV variant distributions used by scorer
committed generator and reviewer skill trees
single canonical external campaign output root
scorer-calibration artifact digest and campaign identifier
freeze_policy.verification: Hash every bound input before each live command; reject a one-byte drift. Existing bound files remain read-only. Freeze must not be written by this offline build.
freeze_policy.after_first_call: Any treatment, roster, metric or analysis change needs a new protocol. Final-eval must not alter frozen inputs.
freeze_policy.optional_vault_commitment: freeze may record opaque --vault-sha256 without reading vault material. It commits to the SHA-256 of canonical JSON {manifest,tasks,dists}; final-eval refuses if the commitment is absent or external vault contents mismatch. Only final-eval opens vault bytes.
freeze_policy.campaign_output: Freeze binds one canonical external DEV output, a separate external final-results root and machine-global spent-ledger location. Every command uses the same DEV root; final split reads only the frozen separate results root. Moving/refreezing DEV output cannot reset consumption of a vault commitment while the external ledger remains intact. Symlink components and repository/cache ancestors refuse.

stop_rules: Only smoke/calibrate may run live without freeze, with --allow-live and non-data outputs. Frozen live commands require --allow-live and matching inputs.
One campaign and one generation/scoring operation at a time on Zeppelin.
Stop on digest drift, another driver, cleanup failure, rate/usage limit, disk below 4 GiB, or inherited three consecutive infrastructure aborts.
Never read eval material except within the once-only external-vault final-eval command after analysis is locked.
Never install dependencies, build variants or mutate the read-only loop cache implicitly; missing prerequisites refuse.
limits: Only two DEV task clusters, both from one PR; repetitions are not independent task evidence.
The heldout screens differ from the stateful DEV screens; a null heldout result cannot demonstrate transfer or equivalence.
The split is deterministic after author task selection; it is not a random task sample.
Pool provenance and previous reference validity remain the pool author's stored claims; no live reference validation was performed in this offline build.
Primary fidelity conditioning is post-treatment selection; primary and as-treated are not randomized comparisons.
Model sign-flip p-values need joint coordinate-wise sign invariance; shared tasks and lineages can violate it.
Parent/child token additivity, child configuration inheritance, allowlist/sandbox enforcement, rollout schema and generation/scoring port behavior require live validation.
Cost denominators with incomplete sessions are excluded and counted; no invented dollar estimates.
No six-synthetic-task results, Claude-family rows, old power table or historical gpt-5.5 rows enter this protocol.

Namespace validation is observational, not a security boundary; transient escaped notes and same-path foreign content edits remain unobservable. Owner must choose stronger proxy enforcement before claiming strict prevention.

The design was exposed to heldout summaries/examples beyond the names-and-counts-only allowance. Fresh workers and vault isolation cannot undo that exposure; registered final tasks are descriptive, not sealed evaluation. Owner approval of design provenance and a new successor with genuinely unexposed tasks are needed for any sealed claim.
Fixed model order and B-after-A timing may confound effects; C retains its scenario-design workflow.
Static selector evidence is class-token-only and cannot measure markup/tag coupling.
Scope scrub regexes reduce public answer-key pointers but cannot certify arbitrary prose, outbound internet or training-data isolation.
analysis_outputs_note: summary re-derives from recorded generation/scoring provenance, writes per-model fidelity/quality/cost, pooled estimates and a freeze/summary digest analysis lock. Offline attribution of candidate failures updates the saved scores before re-analysis.

normalization_rules.scoring_base_url: Only the scratch scoring copy of delivered files has literal http://host.docker.internal:14210 replaced by http://127.0.0.1:14210, identically in all three clean runs, five defect runs and R1. Container generation and host scoring reach the same proxy. Original deliverable artifacts remain byte-preserved; no locator, assertion or test logic rewrite is authorized.
normalization_rules.reviewer_source_namespace: Before B reviewer generation, replace the exact source A cell namespace literal in the copied tests with the B cell namespace. A artifacts remain preserved; B must operate within its own namespace. No other source-test change is made by this normalization.

arm_alignment.plans: One deterministic scrubbed scope-derived official-planner-format plan shared by all arms; bind plans, scopes and prompt suffixes before freeze.
arm_alignment.A_C: Zeppelin frame + exact synthetic PLAN_LINE + unchanged synthetic arm line.
arm_alignment.B: Zeppelin frame with generation-only wording removed + exact synthetic TASK_LINE + REVIEW_LINE; stage_reviewer excludes evals and __pycache__.
arm_alignment.confound: C retains coverage/design workflow; no generator-quality-only claim.

runtime_calibration.before_freeze: Non-model calibrate --allow-live without freeze. Require exact scoring path clean 3/3, R1 pass, expected D1-D5 failing title and reason regex on the same failed test result. Bind PASS artifact at freeze.
runtime_calibration.expectations: DEV task calibration-expectations.json exact D1..D5 -> {failing_test_title,reason_regex}; curator-reviewed, grader-only.
runtime_calibration.drift: DEV drive preserves non-data reference checks at start, midpoint and end as noise-floor evidence.
runtime_calibration.smoke: Fresh external HOME-root smoke --allow-live without freeze, stage/init-agents/bridge reachability/notePath create/delete/list and reference scorer; optional --model adds A/C/B non-data cells.
runtime_calibration.entry: Every synthetically admitted model additionally needs a non-data Zeppelin A delivery and clean entry under the bounded zeppelin_entry_policy. Infrastructure failures stay undecided; valid model delivery or clean failures exclude permanently.

zeppelin_entry_policy.history: Exclusively create numbered attempt directories and immutable started/run/score/outcome records. Starting consumes a slot, including interrupted calls. Never overwrite earlier attempts or retry a valid model failure. Old unbounded entry records refuse.
zeppelin_entry_policy.retry: Only a generation infrastructure failure or interruption can consume the remaining slot on a later preflight invocation. Fatal infrastructure stops permanently. After valid generation, incomplete scoring stays undecided and never launches another model. Exhausted infrastructure budget stays undecided and requires an owner decision for a new successor campaign.

namespace_policy.creation: REST POST uses notePath, never name; UI note creation and rename use supplied folder identically for every arm.
namespace_policy.deletion: Accept DELETE statuses including HTTP 500; retry once and require listing to prove removal. Include ~Trash descendants.
namespace_policy.escapes: Record surviving new IDs outside namespace, delete only those IDs under exclusive ownership, flag scoring run failed, continue. Abort on changes to preexisting IDs.
namespace_policy.conservative_choice: Observational ownership is not strict isolation; transient notes and same-path content edits remain unobservable.

scoring_resume: Completed score/report/freeze digests skip browser rescoring and preserve adjudications. Incomplete matching attempts resume unscored cells. drive --model limits model work; completed matching results skip model scoring/analysis.
source_contamination: Scrub PR/provenance/URLs and source-line pointers from every model-visible scope and plan. Internet remains available in containers, and public tests may be in training data; require independent transcript/rollout fetch audit with per-arm counts and sensitivity exclusion. No network-isolation claim.
codex_configuration_gate: Before live setup, require the unfrozen v4 Codex successor (v3 is a frozen predecessor) arm-A argv danger-full-access, explicit approval_policy never, playwright-test.default_tools_approval_mode approve and the exact 19-tool allowlist. Refuse obsolete adapters and contradictory arm_a_configuration. Frozen predecessor evidence and admission decisions are not reused; no freeze is created by this offline build.
successor_repair_policy: Codex v3 is frozen and preserved. Import the unfrozen v4 runner/evidence. Explicit identity conflicts block every admission fallback and invalidate harness/cost completeness; only a root-linked rollout supplies tool evidence. Safe disposable smoke Git ignores ambient routing/configuration. Fresh admission and live validation are required; no prior frozen evidence is reused.
